pregnenolone.text: Users take pregnenolone because it is the precursor to testosterone, cortisol and DHEA, hoping to support hormone levels and, through them, muscle and leanness. Trials exist for mood and psychiatric uses; a testosterone or appearance effect from supplementing is untested.

chain: Raises fat release from stubborn areas
yohimbine.text: Cutters use yohimbine, often with caffeine and fasted cardio, to target stubborn fat and get leaner in the face and midsection. The alpha-2 rationale is based on mechanism and small studies in athletes; trials in men aimed at visible fat loss are limited.

synephrine.text: Bitter-orange synephrine is used in fat burners and pre-workouts as an ephedra substitute to help users cut body fat. Small trials show more fat oxidation during exercise; long-term fat loss and visible body changes are unproven.

chain: Faster fat loss on a cut
liothyronine-t3.text: Some cutters use T3, a prescription thyroid hormone, off-label to speed fat loss and reduce puffiness around the eyes and face. It is approved for hypothyroidism; use for appearance is off-label and not supported by trials, and the label warns against it for weight loss.

hydroxyapatite-toothpaste.text: Users switch to hydroxyapatite toothpaste as a fluoride-free way to protect enamel and keep teeth smooth and bright. One 18-month adult trial matched fluoride for cavity prevention; whitening claims have thin evidence.

hyaluronic-acid-filler.text: HA filler is injected to add volume and reshape the lips, cheekbones, chin, jawline and under-eye area, so the change in facial contour is visible right after treatment. Its volume effect is well studied, and it can be dissolved with an enzyme if users want to reverse it.

glutathione-iv.text: Glutathione drips are promoted in some clinics for skin lightening and a more even tone, based on lab findings about melanin production. Reviews find limited clinical evidence for this appearance use.

eye-massage-device.text: Users apply warming or vibrating eye massagers hoping to reduce under-eye puffiness and dark circles. Studies have looked at dry-eye comfort; puffiness and dark circles have not been tested.

microneedle-stamp.text: Looksmaxxers press derma stamps into the skin to smooth acne scars and texture and to try to thicken eyebrows or beard areas. Evidence comes from research on microneedling in general and small case series; stamp-specific trials are few.

microneedling-pen-electric.text: Electric microneedling pens are used for acne scars, texture, stretch marks and thinning hair, and are a staple of skin routines in looksmaxxing forums. Small trials support benefits for scars and texture; claims about depth and generic versus branded pens rest largely on user reports.

straightening-hair-brush.text: A heated brush straightens and smooths hair while brushing, giving a sleeker style that is visible straight away and lasts until the next wash. It uses the same heat principle as a flat iron and has no dedicated research.

flat-iron-hair-straightener.text: Users clamp hair with a flat iron to straighten curls or add waves, producing a styled look that is visible immediately and lasts until the next wash. The styling effect is plainly observable, and heat damage is covered in the article.

hair-dryer-brush-hot-air-brush.text: A hot air brush dries and styles hair in one pass, giving volume and a smooth blowout that is visible right away. Claims come from product reviews and the effect is observable without clinical studies.

premium-multi-styler.text: Users buy multi-stylers such as the Dyson Airwrap to dry, curl, smooth and add volume with one device, for a styled look that is visible immediately. Manufacturer claims about gentler styling are untested in published studies.

chain: Hair covers thin or bald areas
wig-lace-front.text: A lace front wig gives a full head of hair with a hairline that appears to grow from the skin, so the change is visible the moment it is worn. It is removable and has not been tested in trials.

hair-system-toupee.text: Men with hair loss use custom hair systems, attached with adhesive or tape, to restore a full hairline and density while worn, a change that is visible immediately. Trials are absent; the scalp-massage hairline claim is untested and based on anecdote.

electric-shaver-foil-rotary.text: Users shave with foil or rotary electric shavers for a clean, tidy face or body, with less redness than blades according to mostly manufacturer research. The shaved result is visible immediately.

cartridge-razor.text: The cartridge razor is the standard tool for a close, clean shave, with the result visible right after. One 59-man study found more redness than with a safety razor.

straight-razor.text: Users choose the straight razor for a very close shave and the ritual of traditional wet shaving, with a smooth result that is visible right after. No studies test its effect on skin or appearance.

shaving-brush.text: Wet shavers use a brush to build lather and apply it to the face, with reference works crediting it with better lather for a closer shave. The shave result is visible straight away; no trials test the brush itself.

shaving-soap-cream.text: Shaving soaps, creams and gels are used to lubricate the skin so the razor glides, leaving a cleaner shave with less redness. The shave is visible immediately; the friction-reduction benefit has not been tested in trials.

threading-kit.text: Users thread eyebrows and facial hair at home for precise, clean shaping, and the result is visible immediately. It is cheap and temporary, and has been little studied.

sugaring-paste.text: Sugar paste is used as a gentler alternative to wax to remove body and facial hair, leaving smooth skin that is visible right after. It is classed as epilation in the medical literature; head-to-head trials against wax are lacking.

hair-growth-inhibitor-lotion.text: Users apply inhibitor lotions after shaving or waxing to slow regrowth of unwanted facial or body hair. The prescription ingredient eflornithine has trial data; over-the-counter versions have little.

whitening-toothpaste.text: Users brush with whitening toothpaste to lift surface stains from coffee and tea for a brighter-looking smile within weeks. It lightens surface stain rather than the tooth's natural shade, and is a low-cost alternative to professional bleaching.

mandibular-advancement-device.text: Looksmaxxers with snoring or sleep apnea use these splints to keep the airway open and sleep better, which feeds into a rested look. It is a medical device with proven use for snoring and apnea and no published research on appearance.

orthodontic-retainer.text: Retainers are worn after braces or aligners to keep teeth straight, protecting the smile people paid to straighten. Retention is well established; claims that they stunt forward growth or can expand the palate with mewing are untested.

palatal-expander.text: Palatal expanders are used mainly in children to widen the upper jaw, and some adults hope they will widen the face and improve structure, sometimes alongside mewing. Orthodontic use in kids is well supported; facial change in adults is largely untested.

orthodontic-headgear-facemask.text: Headgear and facemasks are used in children to correct bite and guide jaw growth, and some looksmaxxers ask about them for a more forward midface. Evidence is in growing patients; adult facial change claims, including with MARPE or peptides, are untested.

herbst-twin-block-functional-appliance.text: Herbst and Twin Block appliances are used in growing teens with an overbite to bring the lower jaw forward, improving the side profile. Research shows modest lower-jaw gain mostly in children; use outside the Class II indication or with home-made substitutes is untested.
